title: Older-data circular fits at 9.8658 days increase later Ross 128 HARPS error under a year-offset model
abstract: We test time transfer among reported Ross 128 period ranges in HARPS-RVBank version 02. Circular waves fitted to 167 older exposures are applied to 138 later exposures. At the fixed published period of 9.8658 days, weighted error rises by 60.2 percent in SERVAL and 31.0 percent in DRS under a year-offset model. Broad period searches favor a longer range on the later data, but narrower ranges and group slopes change rankings. A 1.7 m/s known-period wave is assigned to the correct range in 136 and 137 of 199 conditional noisy simulations; all noiseless checks pass. The result shows a limit of this simple transfer method. It does not reject the known planet or establish a new one. Reductions share spectra, the split spans instrument changes, and no independent-instrument data are fitted. Original code, aggregate evidence, exact input hashes and external retrieval steps are included. External database records are excluded.

display.caption: Older-data wave transfer and conditional recovery of an added known-period wave. Negative gain means increased later error. The two reductions share spectra.
